title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which medical use of Tulsi is mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A cloth
   B. A tool for digging
   C. Tea for coughs and colds
   D. A fuel for cars

2. What should we never throw into rivers? (1 mark)
   A. Rainwater
   B. Rain
   C. Plastic and waste
   D. Clean leaves

3. Which element do we breathe in? (1 mark)
   A. Agni
   B. Prithvi
   C. Jal
   D. Vayu

4. In a maize farm, what does the wind that carries pollen represent among the elements? (1 mark)
   A. Jal
   B. Vayu
   C. Agni
   D. Prithvi

5. A family keeps a Tulsi plant at home. What is a good daily habit for them? (1 mark)
   A. Burn it
   B. Water it every morning
   C. Cut it down
   D. Ignore it

6. Where was Prince Siddhartha born? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Lahore
   C. Lumbini
   D. Varanasi

7. What does Aparigraha mean? (1 mark)
   A. Always be angry
   B. Do not be greedy or hold too many things
   C. Take everything
   D. Talk a lot

8. Sri Guru Ram Das Ji was which Guru of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. The fourth
   B. The first
   C. The third
   D. The tenth

9. Whom did Guru Ram Das Ji serve before becoming Guru? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Amar Das Ji
   B. Guru Arjan Dev Ji
   C. Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   D. Guru Nanak

10. Who declared that Sikhs should follow the Granth as their Guru? (1 mark)
   A. Ram
   B. Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   C. Sigala
   D. Guru Amar Das Ji

11. What does the langar teach? (1 mark)
   A. Equality
   B. Fear
   C. Pride
   D. Greed

12. Which faith does the Dhammapada belong to? (1 mark)
   A. Sikhism
   B. Hinduism
   C. Buddhism
   D. Jainism

13. What promise lesson do we learn from the Ayodhya Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Promises are for kings only
   B. Break promises
   C. Keep your promises
   D. Forget promises

14. What is a prayer? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A way of talking to God
   C. A sport
   D. A kind of meal

15. What should you do with your shoes before entering a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. Remove them
   B. Wear them
   C. Throw them
   D. Carry them inside

16. What could you use to map the Mandirs in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A random guess
   B. A dream
   C. A song
   D. A safe digital map with a teacher's help

17. What should passengers do before boarding a vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. Run alongside it
   B. Jump onto it
   C. Push others
   D. Wait for the vehicle to stop

18. What should you do if you break something at school? (1 mark)
   A. Give it away
   B. Own up
   C. Run away
   D. Blame another child

19. What is a parable? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A kind of prayer
   C. A festival
   D. A short story with a lesson

20. Which is fair play in a game? (1 mark)
   A. Tripping others
   B. Cheating
   C. Following the rules even when nobody is looking
   D. Pushing

21. What should you do if your knees hurt in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. Push harder
   B. Stop and come out of the pose
   C. Stay for an hour
   D. Ignore it

22. Why is yoga best done with an expert? (1 mark)
   A. To finish faster
   B. So no one else can join
   C. To be noisy
   D. To avoid strain from wrong posture

23. In which year was International Yoga Day first celebrated? (1 mark)
   A. 2015
   B. 2030
   C. 1990
   D. 2005

24. Which of these is a way of following Artha? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting food
   B. Stealing
   C. Cheating
   D. Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours

25. What does the Shibi story teach? (1 mark)
   A. A kind person protects the weak
   B. Doves are bad
   C. Hawks always win
   D. Kings do not care

26. Which statement is true about kindness? (1 mark)
   A. It is only for humans
   B. It includes animals and nature
   C. It is only for rich people
   D. It is only for adults

27. What does karma mean? (1 mark)
   A. Action
   B. Water
   C. Wealth
   D. Prayer

28. Which of the five principles is about being born again? (1 mark)
   A. Punarjanam
   B. Prani Daya
   C. Purushartha
   D. Prarthana

29. Which activity is suggested to learn about festivals? (1 mark)
   A. Watch television all day
   B. Copy a friend's essay
   C. Write a composition on your favourite festival
   D. Read a book quietly

30. Which leaves are offered to Shiva on Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. Banana leaves
   B. Tea leaves
   C. Bel (bilva) leaves
   D. Tulsi leaves only

31. What is the abhishek? (1 mark)
   A. Ringing a bell
   B. Lighting a bonfire
   C. Reading a book
   D. Bathing the Shiva Linga with water and milk

32. Which festival comes last of the three studied? (1 mark)
   A. Maha Shivratri
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Yoga Day
   D. Paryushan Parva

33. How should we behave when the National Anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Talk
   B. Stand straight and be quiet
   C. Play
   D. Run about

34. How long is Paryushan in one Jain tradition? (1 mark)
   A. Two days
   B. One month
   C. Eight days
   D. One year

35. What does Madaraka Day teach? (1 mark)
   A. Greed
   B. Cruelty
   C. Patriotism and unity
   D. Pride

36. What is the Indian name for Tuesday? (1 mark)
   A. Shukravaar
   B. Mangalvaar
   C. Somvaar
   D. Ravivaar

37. Which is the largest planet in the solar system? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Mercury
   C. Jupiter
   D. Mars

38. Shani is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Mars
   C. Jupiter
   D. Saturn

39. What is the Panchang? (1 mark)
   A. A prayer
   B. A river
   C. A kind of tree
   D. The Indian traditional calendar book

40. How many days are in the week in the Indian traditional calendar? (1 mark)
   A. Seven
   B. Eight
   C. Six
   D. Five

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write three ways in which a child can practise Prani Daya. (3 marks)

42. Name the three prayers studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

43. State what the Gayatri Mantra asks God to give us. (2 marks)

44. Explain what the white colour, the veena and the book stand for in the picture of Saraswati. (3 marks)

45. Explain the main teachings of the Dhammapada. (3 marks)

46. Explain how the four faiths in this lesson teach integrity. (5 marks)

47. Why is water sometimes used in worship? Give three points. (3 marks)

48. Describe the story of King Shibi and the dove and give its lesson. (4 marks)

49. Give four roles of sacred plants. (4 marks)

50. How can you learn more about the scriptures? Give four ways. (4 marks)

51. Tell the story of Prahlad and Hiranyakashipu in three sentences. (3 marks)

52. Write the meaning of Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva. (3 marks)

53. Compare the teachings of Parshvanath and Guru Ram Das Ji. (5 marks)

54. Describe how to do Bhastrika. (3 marks)

55. Give three uses of the Indian traditional calendar. (3 marks)

56. Name any four of the five great elements of the Panch Mahabhoot. (2 marks)

57. Match each being with a teaching: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha, Guru Ram Das Ji. (4 marks)

58. What do the words Param and atma mean? (2 marks)

59. Give the meaning of Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Tea for coughs and colds
   Tulsi leaves are used in home medicine such as tea.

2. C — Plastic and waste
   Waste harms water and living things.

3. D — Vayu
   Air is Vayu.

4. B — Vayu
   Wind is air, which is Vayu.

5. B — Water it every morning
   Watering the Tulsi is part of caring for it.

6. C — Lumbini
   Lumbini is now in Nepal.

7. B — Do not be greedy or hold too many things
   Aparigraha is non-greed.

8. A — The fourth
   He came after Guru Amar Das Ji.

9. A — Guru Amar Das Ji
   He served the third Guru with humility.

10. B — Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   He was the tenth Guru.

11. A — Equality
   Everyone sits side by side to eat.

12. C — Buddhism
   It is a collection of Buddhist verses.

13. C — Keep your promises
   Ram kept his father's promise.

14. B — A way of talking to God
   We thank God and ask for wisdom.

15. A — Remove them
   Shoes are removed to keep it clean and show respect.

16. D — A safe digital map with a teacher's help
   We can use a map on a tablet.

17. D — Wait for the vehicle to stop
   Wait until it has stopped.

18. B — Own up
   Owning up shows integrity.

19. D — A short story with a lesson
   A parable teaches a moral.

20. C — Following the rules even when nobody is looking
   Fair play is integrity.

21. B — Stop and come out of the pose
   Do not force the body.

22. D — To avoid strain from wrong posture
   Experts correct mistakes.

23. A — 2015
   It was first celebrated in 2015.

24. D — Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours
   Artha is honest wealth.

25. A — A kind person protects the weak
   Kindness protects the weak.

26. B — It includes animals and nature
   Kindness includes all living beings.

27. A — Action
   Karma is action and its results.

28. A — Punarjanam
   Rebirth.

29. C — Write a composition on your favourite festival
   Writing helps us reflect.

30. C — Bel (bilva) leaves
   Bel leaves are offered.

31. D — Bathing the Shiva Linga with water and milk
   Abhishek is ritual bathing of the murti or symbol.

32. D — Paryushan Parva
   It occurs in August or September.

33. B — Stand straight and be quiet
   We show respect.

34. C — Eight days
   Eight days in one tradition and ten in another.

35. C — Patriotism and unity
   It teaches love for country.

36. B — Mangalvaar
   Mangal is Mars.

37. C — Jupiter
   Jupiter is the biggest.

38. D — Saturn
   Shani is Saturn.

39. D — The Indian traditional calendar book
   It lists days, months and festival dates.

40. A — Seven
   Seven days.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give water to thirsty animals, share food, help a hurt friend, do not harm insects, care for plants (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gayatri Mantra, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva and Saraswati Vandana (any correct pair earns 1 mark).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark each, rounded up.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: That the divine light guide our minds toward what is good and true (wisdom).
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for wisdom or guidance of the mind.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: White stands for purity and peace, the veena stands for music and the arts, and the book stands for knowledge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Our thoughts shape our actions, hatred is ended by love, control of anger is strength, and doing good brings peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching, up to 3.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hinduism: truth (Harishchandra). Sikhism: honest earnings (Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo). Jainism: not stealing (Asteya). Buddhism: right speech and not stealing or lying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each faith and 1 mark for a summary.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It cleans, so it is a sign of purity; it is used to wash the hands and feet before prayer; it is poured or sprinkled to show a place is clean and ready.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: A frightened dove flew into the king's lap and a hawk demanded it. The king offered his own flesh to save the dove. The lesson is that a kind person protects the weak.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the dove, 1 mark for the hawk, 1 mark for the offer, 1 mark for the lesson.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen and clean the air; they give shade for rest and prayer; their leaves, fruits and bark are used for food and medicine; their leaves and flowers are used in worship; they remind us to care for life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct role.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to a resource person, visit a temple or library, discuss with friends, watch a documentary, use a safe search engine with an adult (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hiranyakashipu was a proud king who wanted to be called God. His young son Prahlad kept praying to Vishnu. Lord Narsimha appeared from a pillar and defeated the king.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the proud king, 1 mark for Prahlad's faith, 1 mark for Narsimha.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: You are my mother and father. You are my relative and friend. You are my knowledge and wealth. You are everything to me, O God of gods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair of lines, up to 3.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Parshvanath taught Ahimsa, truth, not taking what is not given and not being greedy. Guru Ram Das Ji taught equality, honest work, humility and service. Both teach kindness and care for others.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each teaching set and 1 mark for a comparison.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit tall, breathe in deeply through the nose, breathe out through the nose with the same force, repeat slowly a few times, and rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sitting tall, 1 mark for equal in and out breaths, 1 mark for slow and rest.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fixing festival dates, choosing days for prayers and family events, keeping tradition alive (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: Prithvi (earth), Jal (water), Agni (fire), Vayu (air), Akash (space).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct element, up to 2 marks.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha: God protects the good. Parshvanath: Ahimsa. Buddha: kindness to the hurt. Guru Ram Das Ji: honest work, equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct match.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Param means highest and atma means soul.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: The great night of Lord Shiva.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for great night and 1 mark for Shiva.
